sections.h2: Offices that handle Roane County property tax
sections.html:
A Roane County tax bill passes through three offices, and every one is in the courthouse at 200 E. Race Street, Kingston. Land values come from the Assessor of Property, payments go to the Trustee, and a bill left unpaid long enough lands with the Clerk and Master.

  • Assessor of Property, Suite 5, 865-376-4362: values, ownership updates, greenbelt and tax freeze paperwork
  • Trustee, Suite 4, 865-376-4938 (mail to P.O. Box 296, Kingston, TN 37763): bills, payments, tax relief applications
  • Clerk and Master, Suite 12, 865-376-2487: delinquent taxes after a lawsuit is filed

Owners often assume the Trustee sets the rate or the appraisal, but it does neither. Take a value dispute to the Assessor and the county Board of Equalization, and a rate complaint to the County Commission.

sections.h2: 2026 property tax rates in Roane County
sections.html:
A house inside a city pays the county rate of $1.4523 plus that city's rate, per $100 of assessed value. A house outside every city pays the rural county rate of $1.4987. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25 percent of appraised value.

2026 combined tax rates by location
Where the house sitsTotal rate per $100 of assessed value

Rockwood$2.0788

Oliver Springs (Roane portion)$2.3723

Your parcel's own appraisal and any exemptions drive the real bill. Multiply the appraisal by 25 percent, divide by 100 and apply your location's rate to estimate it.

sections.h2: When are Roane County property taxes due?
sections.html:
October 1 is the due date on the Assessor's calendar. Notices usually go out in late September, and payment is accepted until the end of February. Delinquency starts March 1.

Plenty of owners pay in winter, and that is permitted. Once a house is listed, though, an open current-year bill turns up in the title search and gets paid at closing. Paying in the fall takes one line off the settlement statement.

Payment can be made in three ways. Online carries a convenience fee that the county does not keep. United Community Bank in Kingston and SimplyBank in Rockwood and Harriman accept payments free. Partial payments are taken at the office if you come in person.

Every parcel is valued as of January 1, on a four-year reappraisal cycle whose latest round came in 2025. Between rounds a value changes only if the property itself does, so selling a house does not reset the number.

  • January 1: assessment date for ownership, assessments and tax maps
  • March 15: deadline to apply for greenbelt on land of 15 acres or more used for agriculture or forestry
  • May: assessment change notices go to owners whose appraisal changed
  • June 1: the County Board of Equalization begins hearing appeals
  • October 1: taxes are due to the Trustee

When a notice looks high, phone the Assessor at 865-376-4362 and ask which comparable sales back the figure. If the call settles nothing, carry that information to the Board of Equalization. The filing deadline moves from year to year, so ask the office for the current one.

sections.h2: What tax relief and greenbelt options exist?
sections.html:
Three tools are on offer, and each goes through a different counter.

  • State tax relief for homeowners 65 or older, homeowners who are 100 percent disabled, certain service-connected disabled veteran owners and spouses of a veteran killed in action. The Trustee handles the paperwork, the state decides eligibility, and the income limit changes each year.
  • The property tax freeze, adopted by the County Commission in 2007 under a state program. It is open to homeowners 65 or older under a state income limit, with no more than 5 acres, and the Trustee takes the annual application.
  • Greenbelt, filed with the Assessor by March 15, for farm or forest tracts of 15 acres or more.

Greenbelt carries a price on exit. When land stops qualifying, a roll-back charge equal to the taxes saved over the last three years comes due. A buyer or seller of a farm parcel should ask the Assessor whether greenbelt status is attached before a contract is signed.

Delinquent bills stay in the Trustee's office for 18 months before they pass to the Clerk and Master. A Chancery Court suit follows in March of the next year, with filing fees added and monthly interest still running. Ask both offices which one holds your year. Once the suit is filed, you pay the Clerk and Master and not the Trustee, and partial payments for a tax year are refused.

You can stop a sale by paying everything owed before the sale begins. The Clerk and Master asks for the map, group and parcel number and takes a business or cashier's check, a call to 865-376-2487, or an in-person payment. Call for a total, because interest adds on every month.

The county holds a back tax sale once a year at the courthouse, and the next one is set for March 6, 2027. Property sells as is, bidders must be 18 or older and registered before the sale, and the court must confirm each sale. The usual redemption period is one year from the confirming order. For properties sold at the March 2027 sale where taxes are more than three years delinquent, a law that took effect July 1, 2026 cuts that to 90 days.

sections.h2: Selling a Roane County house with tax due
sections.html:
Request a payoff and settle it from the sale proceeds. While the bill is in the Trustee's hands, that office quotes the figure. After a lawsuit, the Clerk and Master does.

  • Ask which office holds each year, since the answer decides where the check goes.
  • Give the closing agent the map, group and parcel number from your tax bill.
  • If you owe more than one year, request a total as of your closing date.
  • A city lot in Harriman, Kingston, Rockwood, Oak Ridge or Oliver Springs can carry a city charge as well, and the Clerk and Master collects delinquent city taxes too.

A cash buyer who accepts the house as is can close on a short timeline when the payoff is clean. That helps when a tax sale date is approaching.

The county spans 395 square miles. Kingston is the seat, and Oak Ridge is the biggest city. Harriman, Rockwood and Oliver Springs are the other incorporated places. The Census estimate is 57,395 people on July 1, 2025, up 7.2 percent from the 2020 base. There are 26,696 housing units and a 78.1 percent owner-occupancy rate. Median household income is $71,885 and median rent is $785. The county issued 380 building permits in 2025.

faqs.q: When are Roane County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1 is the due date on the Assessor's calendar, and the tax is payable through the end of February. Unpaid bills become delinquent on March 1.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 Roane County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is $1.4523 per $100 of assessed value for city residents and $1.4987 outside the cities. City rates add to the county rate: Rockwood $0.6265, Harriman $0.7024, Kingston $0.8234, Oliver Springs $0.92 and Oak Ridge $1.3784.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Roane County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Trustee's office in the Courthouse, 200 E. Race Street, Suite 4, Kingston, or at United Community Bank in Kingston or SimplyBank in Rockwood and Harriman, where no fee is charged. Online payments carry a convenience fee.

faqs.q: When is the next Roane County tax sale?
faqs.a: The Clerk and Master lists the next Back Tax Sale for March 6, 2027. You can pay delinquent taxes up to the day of the sale, before it begins, to take a parcel off the list.

faqs.q: Can I freeze my Roane County property tax?
faqs.a: Possibly. Homeowners 65 or older with income under the state limit and no more than 5 acres can apply to the Trustee for the tax freeze each year. Call 865-376-4938 for the form and the current limit.
